correctness.rationale: Three same-arm routes and four cross-arm routes are exhaustively enumerated. The gap condition becomes strips in affine coordinates, including its necessary short-branch cut-locus band. Exact planar area sums are integrated for all three tie patterns; the two-equal case gives a positive-measure interval of geodesic multiplicity. Restrictions on epsilon keep all regions in the corresponding rectangles. Independent numeric integration of all route functions at twelve parameter/threshold pairs corroborates each formula, but is not relied upon as a proof.

originality.rationale: Published theta-graph work on one-distance histograms and graph reconstruction concerns only the first, shortest route; the new statistic is the gap to the second distinct simple route, with both a local quadratic correction and a singular atom. The full relevant published statements and proofs were inspected, and neither states this law. General knowledge of all arm lengths permits computing the gap only after an additional order-statistic decomposition; novelty therefore concerns the exact forward law, not the recoverability of arm lengths. The historical search is not exhaustive.
residual_risks: Undiscovered route-redundancy or metric-graph cut-locus literature may contain an equivalent formula under different terms.
Short-distance inversion recovers arm lengths; novelty is confined to the explicit forward second-route gap law, not recoverability.
The reviewed works are not independently priority audited.

value.rationale: Competing almost-shortest paths quantify geometric route redundancy and instability of unique geodesics in a simple multiply connected metric network. The exact tied-arm atom is not a routine scalar shortest-distance moment: it detects a positive-dimensional geodesic branching phenomenon that disappears when the shortest arm is perturbed. The universal quadratic correction and exact all-tie classification make the natural statistic structurally informative.
